notes: New shelf with no old kinds; two planned kinds built as tier kinds (no archetypes). Pill organiser & dispenser: types cover weekly box, time-of-day, travel case, locking/Braille, pill cutter, automatic carousel and connected smart dispensers (Pill organizer Wikipedia). Models: Pivotell range (pivotell.co.uk), Hero (herohealth.com; rated best overall by theseniorlist.com, retrieved), MedMinder and MedaCube (named on theseniorlist.com comparison). No generic weekly-box or pill-cutter brands listed because I found no independent test winner. Adrenaline auto-injector: EpiPen (first FDA-approved 1987; now Viatris, formerly Mylan), Jext (ALK, EU launch 2011), Auvi-Q (Kaléo, voice-guided, FDA 2012; 0.1/0.15/0.3 mg per drugs.com), Adrenaclick (relaunched by Amedra 2013), Emerade (Medeca; all strengths recalled at patient level in UK May 2023 per patient.info and kittmedical, so it may no longer be on sale). Left out: Anapen and other EU brands (maker not confirmed); Symjepi (manual syringe, not an auto-injector); neffy nasal adrenaline spray (not an auto-injector, and not checked this session). No brand entry for Kaléo, Amedra, Medeca, MedMinder or PharmAdva because I did not retrieve a page about those companies. Founding years for Pivotell and Hero Health left blank because they were not confirmed. No traditions apply. No medical claims made.
